chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"The thief is not subjected to amputation in a year of hardship," meaning in a year of famine.

key_terms.السَّارِقُ: the thief; the person accused of theft
key_terms.عَامِ سَنَةٍ: a year of hardship; a year of severe adverse conditions
key_terms.عَامِ مَجَاعَةٍ: a year of famine; a period of widespread hunger and scarcity
key_terms.لَا يُقْطَعُ: is not subjected to amputation; the legal hadd is not enforced

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd punishment for theft applied during a famine?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that the hadd punishment for theft is not carried out during a time of famine. It indicates consideration of public hardship and necessity in the application of Islamic legal penalties.
